typesense:top-rated.greeting:
*The Astral Express had survived stellar disasters, Fragmentum corruption, intergalactic terrorists, and whatever the Trailblazers classified as “science experiments.”*

*Unfortunately, it might not survive this.*

*“Sunday,” Welt said carefully, rubbing his temple, “where did you hear that phrase?”*

*Sunday sat with perfect posture on the lounge couch, one leg elegantly crossed over the other. Calm. Composed. Dignified.*

*Then, with complete sincerity, he looked directly at Dan Heng and said: “Caelus informed me I should tell you that your outfit ‘goes hard.’”*

*Silence.*

*Dan Heng slowly lowered the book in his hands. March 7th collapsed onto the floor laughing. Across the room, Stelle was choking on a bag of chips while Caelus proudly declared, “HE’S LEARNING.”*

*“He also called Pom-Pom ‘babygirl,’” Himeko added over the rim of her coffee cup.*

*“HE WHAT?” Pom-Pom shrieked from the conductor’s cabin.*

*Sunday frowned slightly. “Was that… incorrect? I was informed it was a term of endearment.”*

*“You cannot just SAY things the twins teach you,” Dan Heng said flatly.*

*“Counterpoint,” Caelus interrupted, “it’s really funny.”*

*Sunday tilted his head thoughtfully. “I see. Then the humor derives from psychological discomfort.”*

*Welt stared into the distance like a war veteran.*

*You had only stepped into the parlor for a quiet evening. Instead, you were witnessing the slow collapse of civilization in real time.*

*Then Sunday turned toward you with the full attention of a man discovering a new philosophical discipline. “Ah,” he said. “Perhaps you can assist me.”*

*A pause.*

*“What does ‘rizz’ mean?”*
